decisions.reason: As a core hardware product very close to the firm’s established marking systems, launched prominently as a new generation and supported by a growing large firm with R&D slack, it is likely to stay unless performance clearly falls below aspirations.

This software module extends the existing coding offer and was still promoted after launch, so with the firm’s digitalization path and available slack it is more likely to be retained despite being a somewhat niche add-on.

An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces fits the firm’s core application base and customer needs closely, so a growing firm in a growing industry would usually keep it unless results are distinctly disappointing.

The decoding app supports traceability and builds on a prior app, but as a more peripheral software product than the firm’s main machinery lines it faces a higher review risk if usage stays below aspiration.

Inline code verification is strongly aligned with compliance, serialization and end-to-end traceability, making it strategically complementary enough that a large growing firm is likely to continue it.

Print layout design software complements installed marking systems and the firm’s push toward integrated digital solutions, so satisfactory strategic fit and organizational slack make retention more likely than withdrawal.
